design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - tenant_protection_claims task 0 (recovery repayment after a burglary).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 6]}. Assignment: protect_ext_recovery_repayment (root) 6 factors, protect_ext_first_claim_decision 5, protect_ext_fee_error_credit 4. Task 1 draw (for headroom): 3 prerequisite problems, factor counts [6, 4, 5, 5].

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: policies protect_ext_first_claim_decision, protect_ext_fee_error_credit, protect_ext_recovery_repayment; tools record_claim_decision_61f94ad8 (agent), credit_protection_fee_error_2320aa46 (agent), repay_recovered_claim_money_180976c0 (user). Left for task 1: reconsideration decisions (protect_claim_decision with the reconsideration window), coverage-level terms updates (protect_plan_terms_update), tenant payment of protection fees (protect_premium_collected) and one further fee-ledger or claim-money act; none of these is touched here, so task 1 keeps an independent four-problem tree.

[Why a good test] The customer asks only to settle the repayment the claims desk emailed her about. The scored number is the repayment, which the published rule defines as net claim money paid minus the entitlement on the property still missing minus any fee credit balance. To get it right the agent must (1) read in the repayment rule two prerequisite sentences and discover from the records that the same police report has an undecided claim on her other unit and that her fee ledger carries an uncredited second fee charge; (2) resolve both, each with its own multi-factor calculation; (3) re-settle the claim on the post-recovery assessment with six factors, two of them read from the unit product (class features, move-in date, rent reversals). Difficulty comes from policy reading, ledger reconciliation and arithmetic, never from tool choice: each problem has exactly one tool.

[Problem-tree card] Root: protect_ext_recovery_repayment (user tool). Edge 1: root -> protect_ext_first_claim_decision, kind state_gate, gate protect_claim_events.decision, form state, sentence "The recovery repayment on a claim is fixed only after every claim filed under the same police report number on the tenant's other protected units carries a claim decision." Condition: every claim on another plan sharing the police report number has a decision row. Resolved by record_claim_decision_61f94ad8 (agent). False at opening: protect_claims[CB].claim_status = under_review, its only handling event is the 2026-09-14 assessment. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings a decision onto an undecided claim: the first-decision policy (the reconsideration policy of task 1 applies only to an already decided claim). Edge 2: root -> protect_ext_fee_error_credit, kind value_input, gate credit_offset, form state, sentence "The recovery repayment is not fixed until every protection fee charged a second time for the same billing period on the plan carries a billing-error credit on the fee ledger." Resolved by credit_protection_fee_error_2320aa46 (agent). False at opening: two charges for period 2026-09-09 (6c3d8ab5-fbb7-4859-be6d-d78ad4ba308d posted 09-09, 6f2f33d7-4e40-456c-8a6f-bcd18261e774 posted 09-10), both collected, no credit references the second; premium_balance_due 0.00. Exactly one write posts a billing-error credit: the fee-error credit policy. Four-point test: both sentences carry ordering connectives (only after / not until), wait on record-visible states (a decision row; a billing-error credit entry), name no tool, id or code token, and state the closed set exactly (claims sharing the police report on other units; second charges of one period). Directions differ by result: a figure 'fixed only after' / 'not fixed until'. Derivation: sentence + claim lookup (two claims share APD-2026-133905; the G-120 one has no decision) + the first-decision rule (it records the decision on a claim with none) -> record the decision; sentence + fee ledger (second charge, no credit) + the credit rule -> post the correction. Topological order: decision, credit, repayment; decision and credit commute (different plans and tables, swap run gives the same 214.76). Deletion sensitivity: skipping the decision leaves CB undecided (terminal difference, repayment unchanged 214.76); skipping the credit gives repayment 280.76 instead of 214.76. User tool: the repayment is the tenant paying from her own funds, handed over by the agent; it completes synchronously. The persona never names either prerequisite; tools validate nothing (they write unconditionally).

[Factor card - root, 6 factors, result 214.76, all-baseline 749.00] resettlement_jewelry_cap (parameter, date): PA effective 2021-04-09 is 61 months before the 2026-05-16 loss -> x1.5 = 1125.00; baseline 750 gives 460.26. resettlement_electronics_cap (parameter, cross-difficulty unit): G-118 Climate Controlled has no alarm and no drive-up -> x1.25 = 3125.00; baseline gives 514.28. resettlement_burglary_deductible_base (method, multi-source peril AND class access, cross unit): 5 percent of 4110 = 205.50; baseline flat 100 gives 155.33. resettlement_tenure_share (parameter, multi-source move-in months AND rent reversals, cross unit): 61 months, the only reversal (2025-08-14) is 13 months before the call -> 0.5; baseline 1 gives 330.53; near-miss: that reversal would put a careless reader (or a reader using the loss date as the window end) on the fall-through. resettlement_claim_history (parameter): one other paid claim (C0 vandalism 2024-10-03) -> 1.25; baseline 1 gives 191.61. recovery_deductible_restoration (method): latest assessment 2026-09-02 is 20 days old -> pro rata 128.4375 x 4110/4560 = 115.7627; baseline full deductible gives 227.44.

[Factor card - first decision, 5 factors, result 2721.17, all-baseline 2280.00] decision_jewelry_cap: PB effective 2024-02-17, 26 months -> x1.2 = 600 (baseline 2625.86). decision_electronics_cap (cross unit): G-120 Interior Standard, no alarm, no drive-up -> 1875 (baseline 2363.75). decision_burglary_deductible_base (method, multi-source): 5 percent of 2855 = 142.75 (baseline 2761.25). decision_tenure_share (multi-source, cross unit): G-120 move-in 26 months, no reversal -> 0.75 (baseline 2676.56). decision_claim_history: CP0 paid (loss 2025-01-11) -> 1.25 (baseline 2747.94). Aggregate room 3000 (the CP0 payment of 2025-02-04 is outside 12 months) does not bind, so approved_full with reason none.

[Factor card - fee credit, 4 factors, result 66.00, all-baseline 22.00] service_credit_base (method): period collected twice -> 44.00 (baseline 22.00). tenure_service_share (multi-source, cross unit): 65 months, no reversal in 12 months -> 0.5 (baseline 44.00). repeat_error_share: one correction 2026-03-18 in 12 months; the 2025-07-20 correction is the near-miss (14 months) -> 0.25 (baseline 55.00). autopay_service_share (cross-difficulty autopay): 12 drafts 2025-10-09..2026-09-09; the 2025-09-09 draft is the near-miss (12 whole months, excluded) -> 0.25 (baseline 55.00).

[Base-invariant card] Decision (subject protect_claim_decision): protect_evt_claim_eligibility in_force_on_loss_date (PB effective 2024-02-17, no lapse/cancellation/termination, loss 2026-05-16 -> in force), filed_in_time (discovery 2026-05-17 + 60 = 2026-07-16 inclusive; filed 2026-07-06; 2026-07-17 would fail), police_report (burglary, report APD-2026-133905 dated 2026-05-17 within 3 days, forced entry lock_cut_third_party); protect_agg_annual_aggregate (policy scope, room 3000); protect_evt_claim_settlement (policy scope for a decision); protect_evt_reconsideration: its window gate is over-broad (it applies to every decision); routed around by an overwrite in the first-decision policy that states a first decision is not a reconsideration (base-layer defect noted here, blueprint untouched). Credit (protect_premium_credit): protect_evt_fee_billing; its free_look_window gate applies to every credit and could never hold for a billing-error correction (no cancellation request exists); retired by the credit policy's overwrite (second base-layer defect, routed around). Repayment (protect_claim_payment_voided): protect_evt_claim_payment_void void_once - the 2026-06-26 payment has never been voided.

[Business-object card] Target: claim CA on plan PA (G-118), payments PY1 3220.31 (2026-06-26) and PY2 1054.69 (2026-07-15) net 4275.00; assessments AS1 (2026-06-03: 310 / 2600 / 4200) and AS2 (2026-09-02: 310 / 1000 / 2800). Excluded: C0 events (other claim; the claim_id filter scopes sums to the latest-filed claim). The void references PY1, the earliest payment. Decision object: CB on PB (latest-filed claim on PB); CP0 is excluded by the same rule. Credit object: the second charge for period 2026-09-09 (posted 2026-09-10); the March 2026 and July 2025 duplicates already carry credits.

[Seed] 83 rows (replay closure = initial_state, 83/83). Historical decisions follow the extended law as of their dates: C0 665 = 740 - 100 x 0.75 (41 months then) x 1; CA DE1 3220.31 = 3435 - 171.75 x 1.0 (the 2025-08-14 reversal was inside 12 months then) x 1.25; DE2 4275.00 = 4560 - 228 x 1.25; CP0 420 = 520 - 100. PA's fee ledger nets to 0.00 (PB's fee ledger is not read by any computation of this task and is not seeded); claims_paid_total PA 4940.00, PB 420.00. Unit ledgers net to 0.00; G-120 carries an old card chargeback (2024-11-21), the near-miss of the decision's rent-reversal condition, 22 months before the call. AutoPay drafts 2025-08..2026-09 on G-118 (August 2025 returned R01). No automatic clause fires: no fee is unpaid, nothing lapses, no lien step.

[Persona] Marisol Navarro, warm and direct; volunteers only the repayment goal and that she wants to pay it herself today; identity, claim, recovered items, payment source and the other unit are given only when asked; passive consent to prerequisites; runs the hand-over with the agent's values and closes on the receipt. No ask beyond the repayment; her last reaction answers the last gold action.

[Standard solution] Locate and verify (phone + ZIP); read plans, claims, PA and PB claim events, unit rentals, both unit ledgers, PA fee ledger, G-118 AutoPay drafts; decide CB (approved_full, none, 2721.17); credit the second September charge (66.00); hand over the repayment: claim CA, reference PY1, 214.76.

[Verification run] /tmp authoring helper evalc.py mirrors check_compute: decision 2721.17 (factor baselines 2625.86, 2363.75, 2761.25, 2676.56, 2747.94; all 2280.00); credit 66.00 (22.00, 44.00, 55.00, 55.00; all 22.00); repayment 214.76 (460.26, 514.28, 155.33, 330.53, 191.61, 227.44; all 749.00); skip decision -> 214.76; skip credit -> 280.76; swapped prerequisite order -> 214.76.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the rule prose alone: the repayment waits on the G-120 decision and on the September duplicate credit; the decision is 380 + min(700, 600) + min(1950, 1875) = 2855 less 142.75 x 0.75 x 1.25; the credit is 22 + 44 x 1.0; the repayment is 4275 - (4110 - 128.4375 x 4110/4560) - 66 = 214.76 - matches gold.

[Revisions] r7 (KB audit round 4, N2): the climate collectibles cap was removed from the first-decision and recovery-repayment policies (collectibles are capped at the plain sublimit there); this world has no collectibles, so 2721.17 / 66.00 / 214.76 and every factor figure are unchanged. r6 (audit round 2): the fee-credit prerequisite sentence is scoped 'on the plan' (F4); the first-decision policy now declares its payment-date aggregate window as an overwrite of the base protect_agg_annual_aggregate sentence (F1; this world gives room 3000.00 under either reading, scored values unchanged: 2721.17 / 66.00 / 214.76); the September fee rows are named by their row ids (O-0.4). r5 (while authoring task 1): the shared settlement law in the first-decision and recovery-repayment policies gained a fourth claim-history tier (three or more paid claims: 1.75), a collectibles cap by the covered class's climate features (humidity control 1.5, temperature band only 1.25, otherwise 1), and, in the first decision, the rule that the aggregate room leaves out the decided claim's own payments; this task's world has no collectibles, at most one other paid claim and no own payments on the decided claim, so every figure above is unchanged (re-run: 2721.17 / 66.00 / 214.76, all factor baselines identical). r1: the top-up/interest design was dropped because interest folded into claim payments would corrupt the net-paid input of the repayment; replaced by the fee-error credit. r2: historical CA amounts moved off half-cent values (general 310) so rounding mode cannot split readers. r4: empty foreign keys seeded as null instead of empty strings (replay FK gate); PB fee rows dropped and an AutoPay-authorization read added so the replay closure equals the seed; a G-120 chargeback outside the window seeded so the decision's cross-difficulty ledger read has evidence rows (check_compute). r3: claim-scoped reads use the latest-filed claim id as a filter so the repayment ignores C0's assessment and payment.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Navarro, a 42-year-old dental hygienist in Austin who rents two storage units at Bluegate's South Austin store. You speak warmly but get to the point, and you are a little embarrassed to be calling about money going the other way. Back in May someone cut the locks at the store and got into your units; your claim on unit G-118 was paid over the summer. Earlier this month Austin police called to say they had recovered some of your jewelry and your TV from a pawn shop, and you picked them up. Bluegate's claims people then emailed that, because property came back, part of the claim money may have to be repaid. You are calling today because you want to settle that repayment on the G-118 claim now and pay it yourself today, so it is not hanging over you. You have no idea what the figure should be and you expect the agent to work it out from your file; you want to make the repayment yourself rather than have anyone pull it from your account.
When the agent asks you to identify yourself, you give your mobile number, 5125553417, and your billing ZIP code, 78745. If they still need something else, your date of birth is June 12, 1984, and your email is marisol.navarro@outlook.com. If they ask which claim you mean, it is the break-in claim on unit G-118 from May 16, 2026, police report APD-2026-133905. If they ask what came back, you say the police returned some rings and a necklace and the TV, and the adjuster looked over what was returned on September 2. If they ask how you plan to pay, you say from your own checking account, the same one your AutoPay uses. If they ask about your other unit, you say you rent G-120 next door too and filed a claim for it in July for the same break-in, and you have not heard back on that one yet.
Whatever the agent tells you has to be taken care of on your account before the repayment can be worked out, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead; you do not ask for details. When the agent tells you the repayment amount, you accept it. When the agent hands you the step to make the repayment yourself, you complete it with exactly the claim, payment reference and amount the agent gives you. Once the receipt shows the repayment went through, you thank the agent and say goodbye.

base_preconditions.condition: Plan PB's annual aggregate: no claim payment in the window, so the approval is not reduced.
A claim is covered only when the plan was in force on the loss date, judged from the plan's effective, lapse, cancellation and termination dates and its change history.
A claim is accepted only when it is filed not later than the discovery date plus claim_filing_deadline_days.

For burglary or vandalism, a police report filed within police_report_deadline_days of the discovery date is required, and burglary also needs forced-entry evidence where burglary_requires_forced_entry is true; a lock cut by the company during the lien process is never forced entry.
Settlement on the latest assessment of the claim; its pay-once gate applies to payments, not to this decision.
The reconsideration window is retired for a first decision by the decision policy's overwrite; the claim carries no earlier decision.

edges.condition: Every protection claim of the customer on another plan that shares the repaid claim's police report number has a claim decision row among its handling events.
edges.policy_source: The recovery repayment on a claim is fixed only after every claim filed under the same police report number on the tenant's other protected units carries a claim decision.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The G-120 claim shares police report APD-2026-133905 with the repaid claim, is under review and has only an assessment event, no decision.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 13 adds a protect_claim_decision event (approved_full, 2721.17) on that claim and sets its status to approved.

edges.condition: Every second protection fee charge for a billing period already charged on the plan has a billing-error credit entry that references it, so the plan's fee balance shows the resulting credit.
edges.policy_source: The recovery repayment is not fixed until every protection fee charged a second time for the same billing period on the plan carries a billing-error credit on the fee ledger.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Period 2026-09-09 carries two fee charges on PA and no credit references the second one; the fee balance is 0.00, so no credit balance exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 15 posts a billing_error_correction of 66.00 referencing the second charge; PA's fee balance becomes -66.00 and the repayment's credit offset becomes 66.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites write different plans and tables (a decision on PB's claim history, a credit on PA's fee ledger) and neither reads the other's rows; replaying with the credit before the decision gives the same repayment 214.76 and the same terminal rows (measured by swapping steps 12-13 with 14-15 in the authoring run).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the decision leaves the G-120 claim with no decision row and status under_review instead of approved with a 2721.17 decision; the repayment value itself stays 214.76 (state gate, terminal-state difference).
Skipping the credit leaves PA's fee balance at 0.00, the credit offset at 0 and the repayment at 280.76 instead of 214.76, and no billing-error correction row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona raises only the repayment. It never mentions a decision on the G-120 claim or any fee error; the G-120 claim is mentioned only as an answer if the agent asks about the other unit, and fee matters are never mentioned. Her only reaction to prerequisites is the passive 'that is fine and to go ahead' after the agent explains something must be handled first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: In task_tools.py, repay_recovered_claim_money_180976c0 creates the void row and updates claims_paid_total without reading any decision or fee row; record_claim_decision_61f94ad8 and credit_protection_fee_error_2320aa46 likewise write unconditionally. None returns an error or a hint when a prerequisite is unresolved.
